attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post, reading a WSJ chart and citing his earlier view.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the hedge ('appear') and the Q2 exception. It is an observation about what a WSJ chart seemed to show, phrased half as a rhetorical question. The epistemic hedge 'it appears' signals graded confidence, not a firm assertion.

contract.note: The contract admits the speaker hedged ('it appears') yet scores on a plain reading, which policy limits to firm language. It also swaps the paywalled May WSJ chart, which partly showed projections, for October S-1 actuals the speaker never saw. The result turns on both choices, neither of which the speaker supplied.

evidence.note: S-1 quarterly table, reproduced. In 2025, expenses rose at least as fast as revenue, with ratios of 349%, 253%, 215% and 239%. Consistent with costs tracking revenue last year.
Same table. In Q1 2026, revenue grew 132% while expenses grew 31%, and the ratio fell from 239% to 135%. The break started before Q2, and Q2's marginal pattern was similar to Q1's.
Compute fell from 144% of revenue in Q4 2025 to 72% in Q1 2026, a bigger drop than the later fall to 48% in Q2. The compute measure had already broken from the pattern before Q2.
Confirms Q2 2026 was the first operating-profit quarter. This bears on profit, not on whether Q2 was the only cost-scaling break.

reviews.rationale: On the S-1 figures, the 2025 tracking holds but the break began in Q1 2026, so the contract's terms would yield contradicted. However, the speaker hedged ('it appears') while describing a paywalled WSJ chart of partly projected data. The contract applies a plain reading to hedged language, contrary to policy, and substitutes actuals he did not describe. The hedged reading of the chart is not scored.
